title: 'Dopamine Sites' Let You Shop Without Spending Money
paragraphs: Many people enjoy online shopping. But what if you could enjoy the experience of shopping without spending any money at all? That is the idea behind "dopamine sites," a new online trend that began in South Korea.

Dopamine is a chemical in the brain that is connected with feelings of pleasure and reward. Dopamine sites copy the whole online shopping experience. Users can search for products, compare reviews, add items to their shopping cart, enter a delivery address and even track their delivery. However, no money is ever taken, and nothing ever arrives.

Two examples are Dopamine Shop and FoodNeverComes. On FoodNeverComes, users can order food and even watch a map that shows their food delivery on its way. But as the name suggests, the food never comes.

So why do people use these sites? For many people, the fun of shopping comes from the process, not from owning things. People often use online shopping carts to collect ideas, plan possible purchases or wait for sales. Some people simply shop for entertainment. Some reports also connect the trend to money problems, since these sites let people enjoy shopping without spending money.

Shriram Venkatraman, a researcher who studies digital shopping, said this kind of behavior can be found everywhere. What is special about South Korea, according to Venkatraman, is that it has been turned into a digital service. Helen Jambunathan, a consumer researcher in London, said people now care more about looking forward to things, making choices and collecting ideas than about owning things.

However, some experts are not sure that these sites help people spend less. Psychologist Pamela Rutledge said there is no strong evidence that spending less on these sites leads to spending less in real life. Some experts also worry that the sites could encourage the same habits that lead to shopping addiction.
